messages:
maya: Planning a phased rollout of the new NVIDIA driver (v540.x) + CUDA 12.3 across Dedicated pools. Canaries in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 tomorrow 02:00-05:00 UTC. Main goals: validate p2p+NVLink stability, NCCL allreduce perf, and no unexpected OOMs on long-lived sessions.
ryan: are we still gating on kernel 6.5.x only? some on-prem customers are on 5.15.
sophia: yes, kernel 6.5 is required for the vendor kernel modules we need. we have a compatibility shim for 5.15 but it disables GPUDirect — flagged in the rollout notes.
maya: good call. schedule will skip pools with 5.15 nodes unless they are running dedicated private (on-prem) deployments that opted into the 'legacy-driver' tag. we'll coordinate with SRE to avoid those nodes.
dan: quick question on canaries—how many nodes per region?
maya: 3 H100 nodes and 4 A100 nodes per region. low-util low-cost customer slots only (we'll cordon three non-reserved nodes).
infra-bot: deploy plan created: plan-id=rdo-roll-v540-2026-03-19-01. See /deploys/rdo-roll-v540-2026-03-19-01 for details.
sophia: test matrix: stressgen 30m, p2p memcpy, nccl-benchmark 1k iters, model-run smoke tests (kv-cache warm). we also capture perf counters and power headroom.
ryan: any network-level changes? NCCL 4.x has different socket fallback behavior we've seen before.
maya: no infra network changes. but we will enable verbose NCCL logging for canaries and have an automated check for increased retries or socket degradation.
dan: what are our rollback criteria? latency regressions? errors?
sophia: primary abort triggers: (1) >5% p99 latency regression on generation workloads, (2) any reproducible IPC/driver OOPS/crash, (3) NCCL allreduce failures for 2 consecutive runs, (4) increase in OOMs >50% vs baseline.
ryan: also add a safety: if cost per token changes by >7% due to lower batching efficiency, flag it.
maya: noted. rollback procedure: runbook link https://confluence.internal.redwood/runbooks/driver-rollback (step-by-step). rollback command will be the fleet tool: fleetctl set-driver --pool <pool> --version 539.22 --force; follow with fleetctl drain --pool <pool> --grace 300 and restart serving.
oncall: I'll stand by during the 02:00 window. please ping #oncall when canary starts so we can escalate quickly.
deploy-bot: canary started on eu-west-1 nodes: rdo-eu-w1-n[12,14,18] at 2026-03-19T02:03Z.
maya: first run results: p2p memcpy stable, nccl latency up ~3% but within noise. one node logged a driver WARN right after stressgen: 'GPU watchdog reset attempted' — node rdo-eu-w1-n14.
ryan: what's the warning trace?
sophia: paste log: ```Mar 19 02:15:12 rdo-eu-w1-n14 kernel: nvidia: GPU watchdog reset attempted by process stressgen pid=2142
Mar 19 02:15:12 rdo-eu-w1-n14 nvidia: GPU stuck in reset, attempting recovery
```
dan: single event on one canary node is okay but monitor for repeats. is NVLINK usage high?
maya: NVLINK usage spiked on that node during model-run smoke test. we're attributing to a combination of a long-lived session with aggressive kv-cache prefetch.
ryan: let's abort further canaries in us-west-2 until we confirm root cause.
maya: agreed. pausing us-west-2 schedule. I'll open a bug with priority P1 and tag kernel/driver/nccl. Bug: INFRA-2987.
sophia: triage notes: reproduce locally on a A100 with synthetic load? I can try to repro with the same stressgen+kv-warm settings.
oncall: filing customer notifications: setting status page to 'investigating for dedicated pools in us-west-2' so CS isn't surprised.
deploy-bot: canary in eu-west-1 continuing (remaining nodes) — monitoring.
intra-bot: perf-alert: nccl allreduce retry count on eu-west-1 increased by 18% (threshold 10%).
maya: that's above our abort threshold. initiating rollback on eu-west-1 canary nodes now. executing: fleetctl set-driver --pool rdo-eu-west-1 --version 539.22 --force && fleetctl rollout restart --pool rdo-eu-west-1 --grace 300
ryan: copies. I'll run the post-rollback validation: smoke tests + nccl benchmark.
sophia: assign INFRA-2987 to me. I'll upload logs and attach the kernel oops if present.
maya: postmortem checklist: 1) confirm rollback completed 2) gather dmesg + nvidia-smi from the affected node 3) check customer impact (reserved capacity) 4) update rollout plan with extra telemetry and slower tempo.
dan: also add a preflight check to detect long-lived kv-cache patterns and cordon those nodes out of canary set.
maya: good call. new plan version will add this filter and increase canary size to 6 nodes to improve signal. we'll iterate after Sophia's repro.
ryan: :thumbsup:
maya: thanks everyone — I'll follow up here once Sophia posts repro results and when INFRA-2987 is updated.
